result.question: Compare the Western Ghats and the Eastern Ghats in terms of their relief and continuity, and bring out their influence on the drainage and climate of Peninsular India. (Answer in 150 words)

sentences.text: The Western and Eastern Ghats form the western and eastern edges of the Deccan Plateau, yet they differ markedly in height, continuity and influence.
The Western Ghats are higher and more continuous, and their height increases from north to south.
They are known locally as the Sahyadri in Maharashtra and as the Anaimalai and Cardamom hills in Kerala.
Anaimudi in the Anaimalai hills is the highest peak of Peninsular India, followed by Dodabetta in the Nilgiris.
The Eastern Ghats are low, discontinuous hills, heavily dissected by the Mahanadi, Godavari, Krishna and Kaveri.
The two ranges meet in the Nilgiri hills.
The Western Ghats are the main water divide of the Peninsula, and the Godavari, Krishna and Kaveri rise there.
Lying across the Arabian Sea monsoon, their windward slopes receive heavy orographic rain, while the Deccan interior lies in a rain-shadow.
As a biodiversity hotspot and a source of major rivers, the Western Ghats, like the highly eroded Eastern Ghats, need landscape-level conservation.
